On Fri, Jul 15, 2016 at 10:51 AM, Lvjet <
avrote: 
Jeffrey 
I spoke to Tech ops, John and Mike,. 
Normal PSI in Duct pressure at FL450 (45,000') is 19 to 22psi, it varies with Density Altitude and Temperature 
slightly. 
Mike indicated that Gulfstream does not like the term "Buffet" or "Vibration" they use the term "TRIM Variance" 
if the exhausted air from pylon precooler air modulation valve was not equal to both L/H and R/H the air is 
disrupted over the tail section of the aircraft Causing a TRIM VARIANCE. 
I informed Mike that we had to change the Gasket on L/H anticipator and found a Loose Temp sensor in Left 
Pylon, and we changed the R/H pylon Anticiptor gasket as a precautionary measure. 
Now that Bleed system Duct pressure is tight and equal, Mike feels the aircraft is operating at factory specs, 
Depending on pressurization Bleed system requirements, the Duct pressure will vary when 12th stage bleed 
valve opens for decent. during climb the duct pressure can read as high as 40psi, since the HP Bleed valve located on 
each engine is set to modulate exhausted air at 40PSI max into the cabin,. 
if air was blowing by the Anticipator gasket, this effects the amount of air into the cabin, since the Anticipator is 
anticipating the 400 degree air, and adjust the HP regulator valve accordingly. 
We have changed Both HP Regulator valves about a year ago,. so they are good on both engines.

Opposed to this interpretation, the "will to power" can=be understood (or misunderstood) to mean a struggle against 
one's surroundings that=20 culminates in personal growth, self-overcoming, and self-perfection, and assert that the

My idea is that every specific body strives to become master over all space and to extend its force (its will to 
power) and to thrust back all that resists its extension. But it continually encounters similar efforts on the part of other 
bodies and ends by coming to an arrangement ("union") with those of them that are sufficiently related to it= thus they 
then conspire together for power. And the process goes on.[29J 
It would be possible to claim that rather than an attempt to 'dominate over others', the "will to power" is better 
und=rstood as the tenuous equilibrium in a system of forces' relations to each other. While a rock, for instance, does not 
have a conscious (or unconscious) "will", it nevertheless acts as a site of resistance within the &=uot;will to power" 
dynamic. Moreover, rather than 'dominating over others'=, "will to power" is more accurately positioned in relation to 
the subject (a=20 mere synecdoche <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synecdoche> , both fictitious and necessary, for

Nietzsche <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophy_of_Fri=drich_Nietzsche> = 
Opposed to this interpretation, the "will to power" can be und=rstood (or misunderstood) to mean a struggle against 
one's surroundings th=t culminates in personal growth, self-overcoming, and self-perfection, and=assert that the power 
held over others as a result of this is coincidental. Thus Nietzsche wrote: 
My idea is that every specific body strives to become master over all sp=ce and to extend its force (its will to 
power) and to thrust back all that=resists its extension. But it continually encounters similar efforts on th= part of other 
bodies and ends by coming to an arrangement ("union") with those of them that ar= sufficiently related to it: thus they 
then conspire together for power. A=d the process goes on.129) 
<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_t=_powerncite_note-29> 
It would be possible to claim that rather than an attempt to 'dominate over=others', the "will to power" is better 
understood as the tenuous=equilibrium in a system of forces' relations to each other. While a rock, =or instance, does

other bodies and ends by coming to an arrangement ("union") with those of them that ar= sufficiently related to it: thus 
they then conspire together for power. A=d the process goes on.(29)

In the theory of discrete dynamical systems, a state space is the set of values which a process can take. For 
example, a system in queueing theory recording the number of customers in a line would have state space {0, 1, 2, 3, ...}.

State-space representation <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State-space_representation> - State space (physics) 
<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_space_(physics)> State space search 
<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_space_search> 
In physics <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics>, a state space is an abstract space 
chttps://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space> in which different "positions" represent, not literal locations, but rather states 
<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_(disambiguation)#Physics> of some physical system. This makes it a type of phase 
space <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phase_space>. 
Specifically, in quantum mechanics <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics> a state space is a 
complex <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_number> Hilbert space 
chttps://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert_space> in which the possible instantaneous states of the system may be 
described by unit vectors <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_vector> . These state vectors 
<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_state>, using Dirac's <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Dirac> bra—ket 
notation <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bra%E2%80%93ket_notation> , can often be treated like coordinate vectors 
<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinate_vector> and operated on using the rules of linear algebra 
chttps://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_algebra> . This Dirac 
chttps://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bra%E2%80%93ket_notation> formalism of quantum mechanics 
<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_formulation_of_quantum_mechanics> can replace calculation of 
complicated integrals <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrals> with simpler vector operations. 
See also[edit <https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=State_space_(physics)&action=edit&section=1> ] 
• 
Configuration space <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Configuration_space> for the space of possible 
positions that a physical system may attain. 
• 
State space (controls) <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_space_(controls)> for information about 
state space in control engineering. 
* 
State space <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_space> for information about discrete state space in 
computer science.

In educational institutions, safe-space (or safe space), safer-space, and positive space originally were terms used 
to indicate that a teacher <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teacher> , educational institution or student body does not 
tolerate anti-LGBT violence <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violence_against_LGBT_people> , harassment 
chttps://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harassment> or hate speech <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hate_speech>, thereby 
creating a safe <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safety> place for all lesbian <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesbian> , gay 
<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay> , bisexual <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bisexual> , and transgender 
<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender> students. The term safe space has been extended to refer to a space for 
individuals who are marginalized to come together to communicate regarding their experiences with marginalization, 
typically on a university campus.[2] <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safe-space#cite_note-2> It is criticised by 
many[who? <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Words_to_watch#Unsupported_attributions> ] 
for being contrary to freedom of speech.

<https://www.infoq.com/articles/cap-twel=e-years-later-how-the-rules-have-changed> ) but=unable to get all 3 as they 
mutually assure each other's impossibility= If we add in a fourth parameter at a second layer of abstraction, let'=s call it 
Authenticity, a fifth, Privacy, and a sixth, law enforcement, we=cover the gamut of most of what people care about in an 
internet system. T=ese second three principles form another triangle similar to CAP, they mut=ally assure the other's 
impossibility in some way. 
I think that thinking in terms of these desirable prope=ties in terms of mutually exclusive groups is probably a useful way 
to con=ider the design space. Another well known one is Zooko's triangle: 
=A0https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zooko%27s_triangle. 
In any case, I've gone on a slight tangent. My=point is it's one thing to say you want a new internet because of a 
th=oretical (or not so theoretical) button, it's another to have motive e=ough to actually build such a new network. 
Asides from the button, what pr=perties seem critical to you?

From: Deepak Chopra

To: Michael Shermer 
Subject: Re: My chapter on you 
Dear Michael, 
Your chapter reads well and is certainly more than fair about me, given the general unfairness 
I've experienced from militant atheists and hard-boiled skeptics. Thanks for being so open-minded. 
My only comments have to do with making a difficult subject more accessible to your readers. 
1. I'd slow down at the passage about "redness" and spell out that the brain is dark but we see 
light' the brain is silent, but we hear' the brain contains no pictures, but we see full-blown three-dimensional images. 
Then open up how a neuron works, firing the same chemical signals as any other cell with small modifications. So how 
does a brain cell, born of the same strand of DNA as a stomach o liver cell, think? It seems to me that a brain cell cannot 
think. 
EFTA_R1_01561381 
EFTA02457522
--- PAGE 4 ---
2. On a basic chemical level, the sugar in a sugar cube or the glucose in the bloodstream has no 
special properties; the molecules do not participate in mental activity until they enter the brain. You might want to point 
out this mystery and also note that material monists must show the exact point when molecules exhibit mind•like 
behavior. 
3. Freeman Dyson, among other physicists, cites the mind-like behavior of subatomic particles as 
they "choose" and "decide" what state in the wave-particle duality to exist in. Here's a nice quote from Dyson: 
"It would not be surprising that the origin and destiny of the 
energy in the universe cannot be completely understood in isolation from the 
phenomena of life and consciousness--It is conceivable---that life may have a 
larger role to play than we have imagined." 
"Life may have succeeded against all odds in molding a universe to its purposes. And the design 
of the inanimate universe may not be as detached from the potentialities of life and intelligence 
as scientists of the 20th century have tended to suppose" 
4. You say that choosing between materialist monism and consciousness monism isn't the point, 
but it is. Consciousness monism or "mind first" must show how mind turns into matter. Materialistic monism or "matter 
first" must do the opposite, demonstrating how matter can produce mind. Even though the "matter first" crowd are far 
ahead in scientific acceptance, in fact we see mind produce matter every time a synaptic gap is crossed by 
neurotransmitters or hormones are triggered by experience. A person who is phobic sees a spider and reacts violently at 
the level of stress hormones, elevated heart rate, elevated blood pressure, etc. This physical state is entirely produced 
by a mental interpretation that a harmless insect is cause for panic. 
S. I'm not sure about how you introduce monism. There are famous Western monists among 
idealistic philosophers who are a) not materialists and b) not" Eastern". Since "monad" as a philosophical term is 
associated with Leibnitz, you'll see that it refers to an indivisible "substance," which may seem materialistic, until you 
discover that one order of this substance is the soul. 
"The basic order is three-tiered: (1) entelechies or created monads (448), (2) souls or entelechies 
with perception and memory (419), and (3) spirits or rational souls (482). " 
(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monadology#The_metaphysics_of_The_Monadology) 
Other Western monists who are definitely not materialistic include Spinoza, Hegel, Girdano 
Bruno, and Schopenhauer. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monism#Monistic_philosophers) 
In fact, if you can find a materialistic monist in the West who ranks with these philosophers, 
please mention him by name while acknowledging the main idealistic tradition. 
Thanks for letting me review this chapter--it was very generous. 
Love, 
Deepak
